Dear all,

I am quite new to SEM and I would like to specify some residual covariances in my model which I can do using the  double tilde notation. What I do not understand is why I get estimates for all possible correlations in the summary output even though I did not specify them. Do I have to supress these unwanted correlations in the syntax or what is it that I have failed to understand?

I'm pretty sure this is a basic misunderstanding on my part and if anyone could inform me I would greatly appreciate it.

Here is my sample model and the results. Text marked in yellow is showing the residual covariances that were not specified in the model (I think...).

##############

log.Brown.algae.total ~ log.swm_corr + light

log.Mytilus ~ log.Hard.bottom  + antro 

log.Green.algae.total ~ light +log.swm_corr +log.Hard.bottom

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Specifying residual covariance -strange results in summary
parts:
On 09/24/2013 09:28 AM, Martin Ogonowski wrote:
> Dear all,
>
> I am quite new to SEM and I would like to specify some residual
> covariances in my model which I can do using the double tilde notation.
> What I do not understand is why I get estimates for all possible
> correlations in the summary output even though I did not specify them.
> Do I have to supress these unwanted correlations in the syntax or what
> is it that I have failed to understand?

The following covariances are automatically added to the model (if you
are using the sem() function):

- covariances between exogenous latent variables (lv.x)
- covariances between endogenous observed variables (ov.y)

To find out what lavaan considers to be lv.x or ov.y, type:

lavNames(fit, type="lv.x")
lavNames(fit, type="ov.y")

If you really must suppress these, you can either add fix them to zero
in the syntax, eg

light ~~ 0*antro

or you can use the lavaan() function, where you need to add all your
parameters yourself (perhaps using the auto.* arguments)

Yves.
